messages.author: e19ea506112fd25b
messages.subject: multimodal prior in stan
parts:
Hi,

Does anybody have experience how to implement multimodal prior? Tor example sum of Gaussians. Idea is to determine posterior using huge set of data and then use this posterior as a prior for further estimates. Context is in PK modeling. Posterior is for a large population which will be used as prior for new individuals.

Thanks for any advice,
Linas

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] multimodal prior in stan
parts:
Same way you implement a mixture model for data. See
the manual chapter. I'll add a note that this works for
priors, too!

https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/issues/2122#issuecomment-270966125

Even a simple logistic can be multimodal when transformed
to [0, 1].

- Bob

messages.author: f769d7d2cfcf4edc
messages.subject: Re: multimodal prior in stan
parts:
I've done this. As Bob said, it's the same way you would implement any other mixture in Stan.
Say you have a prior on theta that is a mixture of two gaussians with mixture weights .5 and .5 with sigma = 1 and mu = [-1, 1]:

target += log_sum_exp(log(.5) + normal_lpdf(theta | -1, 1), log(.5) + normal_lpdf(theta | 1, 1));

On Friday, January 6, 2017 at 8:18:51 AM UTC-6, Linas Mockus wrote:

Posterior is for a large population which will be used as prior for new individuals.

Thanks for any advice,

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] multimodal prior in stan
parts:
And if it's 0.5, you can drop the term altogether, because

log_sum_exp(a + b, a + c) = a + log_sum_exp(b, c)

and a = log(0.5) is a constant and Stan only needs the log density up
to an additive constant.

I should add that to the manual, too:

https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/issues/2122#issuecomment-270966125

- Bob
